subject: Nanotechnology
title: Colloidal Synthesis
description: A fast breakdown of Colloidal Synthesis for builders.

hook.text: Heat metal salts in a flask with the right surfactants and nanoparticles nucleate out of the liquid.

buildup.text: Surfactant molecules cap the growing particles, stopping growth at a desired size — nanometer control.

discovery.text: Tuning temperature, time, and surfactant ratio produces particles from 2 to 100 nm with narrow size spread.

twist.text: Scaling up is hard — a flask recipe that works for milligrams often fails at kilogram batches.

climax.text: Quantum dots for QLED TVs are mass-produced via colloidal synthesis — billions of identical particles.

punchline.text: Cook nanoparticles like a recipe — surfactants set the size.

quiz.question: What role do surfactants play in colloidal nanoparticle synthesis?
options: They dissolve the metal salts more quickly
They cap growing particles, controlling their final size
They provide the heat energy for the reaction
